title: Warn in setup when Cargo's bin directory is not on PATH
summary: Setup's Ready step will tell a new user when ${CARGO_HOME:-~/.cargo}/bin was not on their PATH and give the export line, so the README's cargo steps work on a clean machine. Because setup.sh prepends that directory to its own PATH, it must also tell xtask whether the caller's PATH already had it.

defaults_applied.how: Change is Rust in xtask plus a minimal shell marker.
Unit tests for the helper; cargo test and clippy clean.
Criteria check the warning appears or not based on PATH, via tests.
One focused change in setup output.
Detection is code with unit tests, not prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience: a new user running ./setup.sh on a clean machine, then following the README's cargo steps.

xtask cannot see the caller's original PATH because setup.sh prepends the cargo bin directory before exec, so setup.sh must export a marker (e.g. ATHENA_CARGO_BIN_ADDED=1) when it prepends; xtask warns when the marker is set or the directory is absent from PATH.
The existing ~/.local/bin warning (xtask/src/main.rs ~line 410) is the model to mirror.
The warning goes in the Ready step so it is the last thing the user sees.

acceptance_criteria.text: setup.sh (a governance file, changed deliberately) exports a marker whenever it prepends Cargo's bin directory to PATH, in both prepend places, and does not otherwise change behavior.

xtask/src/main.rs has a pure helper deciding whether Cargo's bin directory (from CARGO_HOME, else HOME/.cargo) is missing from the caller's PATH, taking the marker into account, with unit tests for present, absent, unset PATH, and marker set.
The Ready step prints the directory and an exact `export PATH="<dir>:$PATH"` line when it was not on the caller's PATH, and prints nothing extra when it was.
Run `cargo test -p xtask`: all tests pass including the new PATH-detection tests.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean.
README setup wording (if touched) matches the new behavior; CHANGELOG notes the change if the repo convention requires it.

out_of_scope: Editing the user's shell profile automatically
departures: Reference forecast kept; the setup.sh marker adds a small governance-file risk.
